tasks.short: Interpret collective agreements and explain their application to employers and employees.

steps.what: Clarify the question, affected workers and relevant dates.
Find applicable agreement versions, amendments and earlier interpretations.
Compare clauses and draft an interpretation with unresolved questions.

loop.input: Case scope and permission-filtered source pack with version identifiers.
loop.output: Interpretation draft with clause citations, alternatives and missing facts.
loop.check: Verify cited passages exist and match versions; specialist checks applicability and reasoning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved conflicts return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clause interactions and ambiguous language require contextual reading; keyword retrieval cannot settle them.

steps.what: Discuss competing readings and approve the advice within delegated authority.
Send approved advice and file the interpretation with its scope.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted case form in the {WORKFLOW} and index approved agreement versions in the {DOCS}. Deterministic retrieval supplies a source pack to a bounded drafting loop; the specialist approves the interpretation, recipients and release before the {EMAIL} sends it and the {DOCS} stores it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement versions, local amendments and earlier advice are scattered. Applicability often depends on facts absent from the request.
tasks.enabler_now: Version indexing and case forms are established technology. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded drafting can work from cited clauses.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting clauses, national rules and disputed facts still need specialist judgement. Earlier advice may be unsuitable for reuse.
tasks.human_edge: Explain ambiguity fairly, understand bargaining history and recognise when advice needs legal escalation.

ambition.what: An approved agreement interpretation clinic for frontline supervisors.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to searching and filing; more goes to difficult interpretations and supervisor advice. No additional authority to bind either party is implied.

reach.task: Answer routine questions about employment terms.
reach.learn: Agreement coverage, effective dates and thresholds for specialist escalation.

evidence.claim: Version retrieval, controlled drafting and approval routing are feasible building blocks; the digest provides no direct labor-relations implementation.
Generated interpretations need source checks and professional review; savings and accuracy require a local pilot.

assumptions: The company has collective agreements or comparable negotiated employment terms.
The specialist has delegated authority for routine advice and an escalation route for disputed interpretations.
Reusable templates can be portable; confidential employer records remain in an authorised workspace.
Build ranges cover a pilot with one agreement family and existing connectors, not waiting time for legal disputes.
unknowns: Which agreement versions and amendments are authoritative.
Whether earlier interpretations are approved, searchable and reusable.
The specialist's delegated authority and legal escalation route.
Available access, retention rules and consultation obligations under national rules.
research_questions: Can applicability be filtered reliably by worker group, location and effective date?
How often does a source-cited draft miss a relevant amendment or competing interpretation?
new_work: Maintain agreement versions and applicability metadata.
Review citations, ambiguity and recipients before release.
Withdraw superseded interpretations and handle retrieval failures.
Review GDPR safeguards and EU AI Act applicability for the actual intended use.

tasks.short: Prepare disciplinary hearing evidence and help witnesses understand the hearing process.

steps.what: Define allegations, procedural requirements and the evidence collection scope.
Request and collect authorised records while preserving originals and provenance.
Organise evidence into a chronology and identify gaps or contradictions.

loop.input: Authorised evidence collection and provenance log.
loop.output: Cited chronology, attributed statements and possible contradictions or gaps.
loop.check: Require a source location for each entry; distinguish event dates from document dates; specialist verifies material entries.
loop.stop: One extraction per document and one repair pass; unreadable or conflicting items enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative accounts express dates, events and disagreements in varied language.

steps.what: Select relevant material and approve necessary redactions and disclosure scope.
Meet witnesses to explain procedure and clarify their own factual accounts.
Assemble, check and release the indexed hearing bundle to authorised recipients.

tasks.design: A restricted case workspace in the {DOCS} receives authorised records from the {HCM} and {EMAIL}, preserving originals and provenance. A bounded extraction loop drafts a cited chronology; deterministic assembly applies approved selections and redactions, then releases the hearing bundle after a recipient and disclosure check. Evidence judgement and witness preparation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records arrive in mixed formats, provenance is recorded manually and each hearing has different disclosure requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexing, access controls and bundle generation are established. Bounded extraction can reduce the first pass through narrative evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, relevance, fair disclosure and witness welfare require professional judgement. Poor records cannot be repaired by generating a plausible account.
tasks.human_edge: Prepare witnesses without shaping their testimony, test competing accounts and protect procedural fairness.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less bundle assembly and more evidence checking and witness support. Authority over disciplinary outcomes does not change.

reach.task: Collect and organise disciplinary case records.
reach.learn: Provenance, preservation, access restrictions and disclosure procedures.

reach.task: Review whether a disciplinary process treats participants fairly.
reach.learn: How to distinguish procedural concerns from findings about the allegation.

evidence.claim: Controlled collection, cited chronology extraction and deterministic bundle assembly are feasible; no direct hearing-preparation case appears in the digest.
Witness preparation and evidence relevance require human judgement; generated material must remain distinct from original evidence.

assumptions: The specialist prepares the case but does not automatically decide the disciplinary outcome.
Only records within an approved collection scope are accessible.
No automated credibility, emotion or worker-risk scoring is introduced.
Build ranges cover one procedure and a limited set of document formats.
unknowns: Applicable national rules, representation rights and disclosure deadlines.
Where original evidence resides and whether it can be exported with provenance.
Who approves evidence selection, redactions and disclosure.
Whether existing processing includes employee monitoring or special-category data.
research_questions: Does extraction preserve attribution, uncertainty and contradictions across representative case files?
Can exported bundles prove that redactions removed underlying text and metadata?
Which GDPR assessment and employee consultation steps apply to the proposed processing?
new_work: Handle unreadable records, duplicate versions and missing provenance.
Test redactions and access permissions before disclosure.
Maintain preservation, retention and deletion rules.
Maintain approved witness process guidance without generating testimony.

tasks.short: Mediate between employer and employee representatives to reconcile differences.

steps.what: Arrange participation, availability and confidentiality expectations.
Read each party's submission and prepare a neutral agenda.
Facilitate discussion, explore interests and test possible resolutions.
Record proposed terms and obtain each party's explicit agreement.
Record agreed actions, send reminders and arrange follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling and approved reminders through the {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. A deterministic agenda and resolution generator in the {DOCS} uses structured fields entered by the specialist, with separate access for private notes and shared terms. Parties approve the resolution, and the specialist approves action owners, recipients and reminders before follow-up begins.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most value comes from a trusted conversation. Small administrative savings were fragmented across scheduling, notes and follow-up.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, templates and reminders can cover the administrative work. A small amount of integration makes them usable together without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Power imbalances, trust, confidential disclosures and willingness to compromise remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what parties mean, manage tension and recognise whether agreement is informed and voluntary.
tasks.altitude: Most of the week still involves preparation and mediation. Administrative effort falls modestly; settlement authority remains with the parties.

reach.task: Follow through on actions agreed during mediation.
reach.learn: Confidentiality boundaries, voluntary agreement and escalation when commitments fail.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, structured document generation and reminders can support mediation without automating the conversation.
The digest provides no direct mediation automation case; substantial time savings are not established.

assumptions: The specialist acts as an accepted facilitator within the company's process.
The parties retain authority to accept or reject proposed terms.
Preparation uses structured templates; reading sensitive submissions remains human.
The solution does not record or analyse the mediation conversation.
unknowns: Whether the specialist is sufficiently independent for the proposed mediation.
Which notes can be retained or shared under national rules and participation terms.
How each party confirms agreement and who can commit the employer.
Whether consultation is required for the proposed recordkeeping changes.
research_questions: Which administrative steps actually delay mediation in representative cases?
Can existing access controls keep private preparation notes separate from shared resolutions?
new_work: Maintain neutral templates and participation terms.
Check shared recipients and keep private notes restricted.
Handle declined appointments and failed reminders.
Check completion of agreed actions without exposing confidential discussion.

tasks.short: Check wages, hours and employment practices against collective agreements and resolve exceptions.

steps.what: Identify applicable clauses, worker groups and effective dates.
Export relevant pay, working-time and employment records.
Reconcile records and calculate deviations from contractual requirements.
Investigate flagged cases and distinguish breaches from valid exceptions or missing data.
Agree corrective action, ownership and timing with the responsible manager.
Record remediation status and check subsequent records for recurrence.

tasks.design: Approved, effective-dated checks in the {WORKFLOW} drive scheduled, read-only extracts from the {HCM} and {PAYROLL} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic reconciliations populate an exception dashboard in the {BI}, linking each flag to records and agreement clauses in the {DOCS}. Specialists validate findings and managers approve remediation; the workflow tracks closure without changing pay or employment terms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement scope, pay codes and worker groups rarely align cleanly. Manual exports and reconciliations make repeated checks expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled extracts and rule engines are established technology. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings, checks and exception views; no model is needed for approved arithmetic rules.
tasks.still_hard: Translating ambiguous clauses into testable rules, incomplete working-time records and national exceptions remain difficult. A clean dashboard does not prove overall compliance.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a deviation is a breach, understand its effect on workers and negotiate proportionate correction.

ambition.what: Daily triage of new wage-and-hours exceptions before payroll cut-off.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling samples to validating exceptions and preventing repeat breaches. The specialist can prioritise investigations, while pay changes remain subject to existing approval rights.

reach.task: Reconcile pay adjustments and verify corrections in the next pay run.
reach.learn: Pay-code mapping, effective dating and control totals.

reach.task: Check whether pay structures implement negotiated terms.
reach.learn: Agreement coverage, allowance interactions and auditable rule specifications.

evidence.claim: Deterministic joins, calculations and exception dashboards can check explicit contractual rules; the digest provides no direct implementation for this occupation.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment where a system makes solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
In the Netherlands, works council consent rights cover specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require assessment under national rules.

assumptions: Relevant working-time records are available through the {HCM} or an authorised linked export.
Today, a spreadsheet commonly joins the exports; companies with existing controls should configure those first.
The initial scope contains explicit wage, allowance and hours checks, not automated worker evaluation.
Build ranges cover one agreement family and two accessible source systems; consultation ranges are effort estimates, not guaranteed elapsed time.
The GDPR and EU AI Act apply; intended use determines the specific obligations.
unknowns: Whether existing systems already implement the required checks.
Availability and refresh frequency of working-time and pay data.
Agreement coverage, pay-code mappings and authorised exceptions.
Applicable national consultation requirements and whether Dutch works council rules apply.
Whether the design constitutes employee monitoring or another processing activity requiring a DPIA.
research_questions: Which clauses can be expressed as deterministic checks with agreed examples?
Do historical reconciliations reproduce known corrections without excessive false flags?
Does the intended use require additional GDPR or EU AI Act controls?
Can daily source refreshes support useful action before payroll cut-off?
new_work: Approve and version contractual checks and effective dates.
Maintain source mappings and investigate failed reconciliations.
Review new exceptions and record reasons for closure.
Check that closed findings remain corrected in subsequent records.
Maintain access controls, processing assessments and consultation records where required.

role.altitude: The role spends less time finding records, assembling bundles and reconciling exports. More time goes to contested interpretations, fair hearings, mediation and preventive action; bargaining and employment decision rights remain unchanged.
reach: Support human resources specialists with approved interpretations of negotiated terms.
Help payroll clerks connect contractual findings to verified pay corrections.
Help human resources managers follow through on agreed resolutions without exposing confidential discussions.
skills_to_grow: Translate explicit agreement clauses into testable, effective-dated checks.
Verify source citations, provenance and document redactions.
Design restricted case records and clear approval boundaries.
Understand GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and consultation under national rules.
Strengthen mediation, witness preparation and explanation of uncertainty.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an approved interpretation clinic for frontline supervisors and timely contract-exception triage before payroll cut-off. Keep substantive advice, disclosure, settlements and employment actions under accountable human control.
